proposal.mixer_type: T-junction (O2 gas into liquid stream between Stage 1 and Stage 2 coils)
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan mixing_order_reasoning: All liquid reagents (stream A) are pre-mixed offline in the dark — no reaction occurs without light, so PMPSCH2TMS, acrylonitrile, and Ir catalyst are stable together in solution. This single-feed approach avoids any premixing issues. O2 (stream B) is introduced only at the inter-stage T-junction, after the Stage 1 anaerobic coil outlet and before Stage 2 coil inlet. This is the critical sequencing requirement: O2 would quench the alpha-thio carbon radical in Stage 1, destroying Giese selectivity. The T-junction gas-liquid mixing point is positioned between the two reactor coils, both of which are irradiated under the same 450 nm UV-150 module.
pre_reactor_steps: OFFLINE DEGASSING (mandatory, hard constraint): Prepare the EtOH/pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v) solvent mixture and dissolve all reagents (PMPSCH2TMS 1.0 equiv, acrylonitrile 2.0 equiv, Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 0.5 mol%) to give 0.1 M solution. Sparge the sealed reservoir with dry argon for ≥20 min. Cap and maintain under Ar positive pressure throughout Stage 1. No inline degasser is available or permitted (hard constraint Q-CONSTR-001).

RESERVOIR SEALING: Transfer degassed solution to a sealed syringe reservoir or Schlenk-type vessel under Ar. Connect to pump inlet via Ar-purged transfer line. Verify no headspace O2 before starting flow.

LIGHT SOURCE WARM-UP: Power on Vapourtec UV-150 450 nm module (KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450) and allow LED to stabilize for 5 min before starting flow. Set UV-150 to additional cooling mode to achieve 25°C (within 10–35°C additional cooling range per photoreactor_limits).

SYSTEM PRIMING (Stage 1): Prime Stage 1 PFA 10 mL coil with degassed solution at 0.167 mL/min under Ar atmosphere. Allow 3× τ (3 × 60 min = 180 min) startup waste (~30 mL) before collecting. Note: startup waste is high due to large reactor volume; this is acceptable for a maximized-yield screening run.

MFC VERIFICATION: Set Bronkhorst O2 MFC to 1.12 sccm. Verify MFC outlet pressure compatible with BPR setpoint (7 bar). Do not open O2 to reactor until Stage 1 priming is complete and steady-state confirmed.
post_reactor_steps: BPR PRESSURE HOLD: Maintain 7 bar BPR (KHU-BPR-FIXED-7BAR) downstream of Stage 2 coil throughout collection. This keeps O2 dissolved during Stage 2 (Henry's law) and prevents acrylonitrile degassing (bp 77°C).
COLLECTION: Collect product stream in a sealed vial under ambient atmosphere after BPR. Product is sulfoxide 4a in EtOH/buffer mixture.
LIGHT OFF / MFC OFF: After collection complete, turn off UV-150 module and close O2 MFC before flushing system. Flush with degassed EtOH to clear lines.

ANALYTICAL WORKUP: Dilute collected fraction for HPLC or NMR analysis. Compare to batch benchmark (95% yield sulfoxide 4a). Check for sulfide 3a intermediate (indicates incomplete Stage 2 oxidation — increase τ or O2 flow if present) and PMPSCH3 byproduct (indicates insufficient pH buffering).
proposal.chemistry_notes:
MECHANISM: Stage 1 (Giese radical addition, anaerobic): Ir(III) photoexcited to Ir(III)* at 450 nm → oxidative quenching SET with PMPSCH2TMS → alpha-thio carbon radical → Giese addition to acrylonitrile → adduct radical reduced by Ir(II) → sulfide 3a. O2 MUST be excluded — O2 traps carbon radicals faster than acrylonitrile addition (k_O2 ~10^9 M^-1s^-1). Stage 2 (aerobic oxidation): Ir(III)* sensitizes triplet O2 to singlet O2 via energy transfer (MLCT triplet energy ~60 kcal/mol >> singlet O2 at 22.5 kcal/mol) → singlet O2 oxidizes sulfide 3a to sulfoxide 4a. Both stages require 450 nm light and the same Ir catalyst. pH 9 buffer suppresses protodesilyation/PMPSCH3 byproduct. ANALOGY ANALYSIS: Analogy 1 (score 0.550): Chemically similar — Ir photoredox catalysis, radical addition, same catalyst metal class (Ir(ppy) family), same temperature (25°C). Key difference: Analogy 1 used fac-Ir(ppy)3 (reductive quenching) in DMSO, achieved 30 min residence time with 48x batch reduction from 24h batch. Our reaction uses Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)+ (oxidative quenching, stronger oxidant) in EtOH/water, 10h batch. Adjustment: the batch time ratio suggests similar flow intensification; 30 min from analogy directly applicable as Stage 1 residence time starting point. We use 60 min for Stage 1 (2x longer) to bias toward maximized conversion per design objective, accepting that analogy suggests 30 min may suffice. Analogy 2 (score 0.537): Chemically similar — same exact photocatalyst class Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6, SET mechanism, blue LED 440 nm. Key difference: different reaction (cross-coupling with Ni co-catalyst, not Giese), DMF solvent, 50°C flow temperature vs 25°C batch. 12 min residence time at 0.83 mL/min in 10 mL FEP. Adjustment: our reaction is at 25°C (same as our batch), same catalyst family, but different reaction type — 12 min is too short for our more complex two-stage chemistry. Analogy 3 (score 0.507): Chemically similar — 450 nm blue LED, radical addition photocatalysis, 25°C, Ar atmosphere, same concentration 0.1 M. Key difference: 2-benzopyrylium catalyst (not Ir), 1,2-dichloroethane solvent, achieved 2.5 min from 60 min batch (24x IF). Adjustment: 24x IF is consistent with our calculated 21x IF; validates the intensification factor estimate. However, reaction is simpler (single step, no gas-liquid stage). REACTOR CHOICE RATIONALE: Two-stage design uses the 10 mL PFA coil (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) for Stage 1 (anaerobic Giese, τ=60 min at 0.167 mL/min) in the UV-150 with 450 nm module. For Stage 2 (aerobic oxidation), the 10 mL FEP coil (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-10ML) is used with O2 segmented flow, also under UV-150 450 nm. CONSTRAINT CHECK: UV-150 maximum coil volume = 10 mL per cartridge slot. If only one UV-150 slot is available, Stage 1 (10 mL PFA) uses UV-150 and Stage 2 (10 mL FEP) uses the KHU manual photoreactor (448 nm, 62 mW/cm2, 40°C with fan) as a lower-intensity alternative — this is a feasible fallback but may require longer τ for Stage 2. Primary design assumes two UV-150 slots or serial coil arrangement. TEMPERATURE: 25°C required (batch protocol, all analogies). UV-150 additional cooling mode (10–35°C range) achieves this. PRESSURE: BPR at 7 bar maintains O2 solubility in Stage 2 and suppresses acrylonitrile volatility. 7 bar > calculated 3.3 bar requirement, provides adequate safety margin. FLOW REGIME: Re=7.8 (laminar, confirmed plug flow Pe=329). Da=1.75 (transition zone — mixing may limit; noted in engineering calculations). Conservative τ=60 min selected partly to address this. PUMP: Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump (KHU-PUMP-VAPOURTEC-R-SERIES) selected for stream A — compatible with UV-150 system, handles EtOH/aqueous mixtures, 0.01–10 mL/min range covers 0.167 mL/min, max 42 bar >> operating pressure.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Calculation range: 11.1–150.0 min (blended analogy IF=21x). Analogy 1 gives 30 min (48x IF from 24h batch, Ir photoredox radical addition at 25°C — directly applicable mechanism). Analogy 3 gives 2.5 min (24x IF, but simpler single-step reaction). Calculation central estimate τ=28.6 min. Design objective is MAXIMIZED CONVERSION, so we select τ=60 min (upper-conservative within range) to ensure >95% conversion matching batch yield, given: (a) Da=1.75 warning from mixing calculations, (b) two-step sequential chemistry requiring both steps to reach completion, (c) kinetics uncertainty (6x vs 21x IF disagreement). 60 min is 2x analogy 1 value — conservative but justified for maximized yield objective. Total two-stage τ=120 min vs 10h batch = 5x intensification (conservative vs calculated 21x — appropriate given uncertainty).
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Liquid-only volume / liquid flow rate. In Stage 2 with gas-liquid segmented flow, the liquid occupies ~29% of channel (ε_g=0.71 from calculations), so actual liquid residence time in Stage 2 channel is longer per unit reactor volume, but the reported value uses nominal V_R/Q_liq for simplicity and safety margin. In-channel pressure-corrected time is slightly shorter (~55 min) due to gas compression at 7 bar BPR.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: 25°C — directly from batch protocol (hard constraint) and all three analogies (all operate at 25°C). UV-150 additional cooling mode achieves 10–35°C range, so 25°C is reachable. No thermal advantage gained by increasing temperature for this photoredox reaction; photon flux is the rate-limiting factor.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Engineering calculation: BPR required = 3.3 bar (gas-liquid system). Available fixed BPR options: 1.5, 2.5, 7.0, 8.0, 16.0 bar. Nearest above 3.3 bar is 7.0 bar (KHU-BPR-FIXED-7BAR). Selected 7.0 bar: (a) above minimum 3.3 bar requirement, (b) provides additional O2 solubility enhancement (Henry's law: higher pressure = more dissolved O2 for Stage 2 oxidation), (c) suppresses acrylonitrile volatility (bp 77°C at 1 bar; at 7 bar dissolved), (d) well within pump max 42 bar. Total system pressure = BPR 7 bar + ΔP 2.76 bar = 9.76 bar — within Vapourtec R-series 42 bar limit. MFC outlet max 9 bar — compatible with 7 bar BPR operating pressure.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: Stage 1: PFA (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) — UV-transparent, max 80°C, max 34 bar, compatible with UV-150 cartridge (≤10 mL). PFA preferred over FEP for UV-150 because max T=80°C vs FEP 50°C, giving better thermal headroom. Stage 2: FEP (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-10ML) — UV-transparent, suitable for gas-liquid O2 segmented flow, max 50°C adequate for 25°C operation. FEP has slightly better O2 permeability than PFA which is a minor benefit for aerobic stage. Both materials chemically compatible with EtOH/aqueous/acrylonitrile/TMS silane reagents.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.1 M — directly from batch protocol. Analogy 1: concentration not specified. Analogy 2: 0.05 M (lower, but different reaction type). Analogy 3: 0.1 M (exact match). No adjustment needed; 0.1 M is appropriate for photoredox catalysis at this scale, gives adequate photon penetration at 1 mm ID (Beer-Lambert: absorbance at 0.1 M with Ir loading 0.0005 M is dominated by substrate transparency at 450 nm).
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 has MLCT absorption with tail to ~460 nm; peak excitation ~380 nm but significant absorption at 450 nm. Batch uses 452 nm 10W LED. UV-150 450 nm module (measured 450 nm) at 355 mW/cm2 is the best inventory match — 35.5x higher irradiance than batch (10W over pressure tube ~10 mW/cm2 estimated) combined with ~20x higher S/V ratio = ~700x more photons per molecule. This drives the predicted 21x residence time reduction. No other UV-150 module is closer to 452 nm with comparable power (470 nm is off-peak; 420 nm is 30 nm blue-shifted but still on MLCT tail at 243 mW/cm2 — secondary option if 450 nm unavailable).
reasoning_per_field.deoxygenation_method: Hard constraint: no inline degasser permitted. Only allowed method: pre-degassed solvent offline. Ar sparge ≥20 min reduces dissolved O2 to <0.1 ppm (literature validated for similar aqueous/EtOH systems). Sealed Ar reservoir maintained throughout Stage 1. This is sufficient for Stage 1 radical chemistry.

explanation:
# Flow Chemistry Design: Photoredox Giese Addition / Aerobic Sulfide Oxidation

---

## (1) Proposed Flow Setup

**Overall architecture:** Two-stage continuous flow, single liquid pump + O₂ MFC, series coil reactors under 450 nm irradiation.

### Hardware
| Item | Specification |
|------|--------------|
| Pump | Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump |
| Stage 1 reactor | PFA coil, 1.0 mm ID, 10 mL (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) in Vapourtec UV-150 450 nm module |
| Stage 2 reactor | FEP coil, 1.0 mm ID, 10 mL (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-10ML), same 450 nm module (second slot) or manual blue photoreactor (448 nm, 62 mW/cm², 40 °C) as fallback |
| Light source | Vapourtec UV-150, 450 nm measured, 24 W radiant, 355 mW/cm² — set to additional cooling mode for 25 °C |
| O₂ feed | Bronkhorst MFC, setpoint **0.8101 sccm** (0.1118 mL/min actual at line pressure) |
| BPR | Fixed 3.0 bar downstream of Stage 2 |
| Inter-stage junction | T-piece between Stage 1 outlet and Stage 2 inlet — O₂ introduced here only |

### Operating Parameters
| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Temperature | 25.0 °C |
| Liquid flow rate | 0.36145 mL/min |
| Reactor volume (liquid-basis) | 3.9281 mL total |
| Residence time (liquid-only basis) | **8.3 min** |
| Residence time at inlet (pressure-corrected) | 3.35 min |
| Concentration (limiting reagent) | 0.1 M |
| BPR | 3.0 bar |
| Wavelength | 450.0 nm |
| Gas holdup (Stage 2) | 0.2363 (23.6% of channel volume) |

### Feed Preparation (Stream A — single pre-mixed feed)
Dissolve in EtOH / pH 9 aqueous buffer (5:1 v/v) in a sealed reservoir:
- PMPSCH2TMS (1a) — 0.1 M, 1.0 equiv
- Acrylonitrile (2a) — 0.2 M, 2.0 equiv
- Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ — 0.5 mol%

**Sparge with dry Ar ≥ 20 min. Seal under Ar positive pressure. Maintain throughout Stage 1.**

### Stream B — O₂ gas
Pure O₂ via MFC at **0.8101 sccm**, introduced at T-junction between Stage 1 and Stage 2 only.

### Process flow (abbreviated)
Degassed reservoir → pump (0.36145 mL/min) → Stage 1 PFA coil (UV-150, 450 nm, 25 °C, anaerobic) → T-junction + O₂ MFC → Stage 2 FEP coil (450 nm, 25 °C, gas–liquid segmented flow) → fixed BPR (3.0 bar) → collection.

---

## (2) Why These Conditions Were Chosen

### Mechanistic basis for two-stage design
**Stage 1 (Giese radical addition, anaerobic):** Ir(III) is photoexcited at 450 nm → oxidative quenching SET with PMPSCH2TMS generates an α-thio carbon radical → Giese addition to acrylonitrile → reductive termination gives sulfide intermediate 3a. O₂ must be absent: O₂ quenches carbon radicals at ~10⁹ M⁻¹s⁻¹, faster than radical addition to acrylonitrile.

**Stage 2 (aerobic sulfoxidation):** The same Ir catalyst, still under 450 nm light, sensitizes dissolved O₂ to singlet ¹O₂ via triplet energy transfer (Ir MLCT triplet ~60 kcal/mol ≫ ¹O₂ energy gap 22.5 kcal/mol). Singlet O₂ oxidises sulfide 3a → sulfoxide 4a. Both stages use identical photocatalyst and wavelength; the only variable is the presence or absence of O₂.

### Literature analogies used to set residence time and conditions

**Analogy 1** — Ir(ppy)₃-catalysed photoredox radical addition in flow, 25 °C, 24 h batch → 30 min flow (48× batch compression). Mechanism directly comparable (Ir photoredox, radical addition, same temperature). This sets 30 min as a credible upper-end anchor for Stage 1. The present design uses **8.3 min liquid residence time** across both stages combined, which is more aggressive; the screen matrix (S1–S5, 10–30 min range) is intended to bracket the true optimum before committing.

**Analogy 2** — Ir[dF(CF₃)ppy]₂(dtbbpy)PF₆ photoredox flow (same catalyst class, 440 nm, 12 min at 0.83 mL/min in 10 mL FEP coil). Different reaction type (Ni/Ir dual catalysis, DMF, 50 °C), so the 12 min value is not directly portable, but it confirms the catalyst class is productive in flow at sub-30 min residence times.

**Analogy 3** — 450 nm blue LED, radical addition photocatalysis, 25 °C, Ar atmosphere, 0.

**Confidence: MEDIUM** — Best analogy score: 0.55. A related literature precedent was found but conditions differ. Validate key parameters (residence time, concentration) experimentally.

Final engineering validation: screen_required.

Final design disposition: BLOCK. Blocked by 5 deterministic hard-feasibility failure(s); do not execute the proposed experiment.

The Vapourtec UV-150 450 nm module (measured 450 nm, 24 W radiant, 355 mW/cm²) is the best inventory match — it provides the highest radiant power among blue modules and matches the catalyst absorption. This module is compatible with ≤10 mL PFA coils in the UV-150 system.
chemistry_plan.confidence_notes: 1. The exact mechanism (oxidative vs reductive quenching in Step 1, energy transfer vs SET for singlet O2 in Step 2) is inferred from the catalyst properties and literature precedent — not measured for this specific substrate. 2. O2 stoichiometry (2.0 equiv) is an estimate; actual MFC setpoint will need optimization. 3. The batch protocol specifies 25 °C; the UV-150 standard range is 35–80 °C (additional cooling needed to reach 25 °C, which is within the 10–35 °C additional cooling range). 4. Acrylonitrile volatility (bp 77 °C) means a BPR is advisable to maintain it in solution, especially with gas-liquid segmented flow in Stage 2. 5. The two stages both require 450 nm light — if only one UV-150 is available, the two coils must be arranged in the same UV-150 housing (≤10 mL total), or one stage uses the manual photoreactor (448 nm, but only 40 or 50 °C).

intensification_mandate.flow_justification_basis: Predicted screening target: 20.0x residence-time reduction; this is a hypothesis unless the run explicitly selects the intensify policy. Identified batch limitations: mass_transfer_gas_liquid, photon_penetration. Primary flow advantage: mass_transfer. Mechanisms: gas-liquid kLa enhancement (segmented flow), photon penetration via small ID, selectivity-sensitive stream logic. Limitation-driven IF (20x) exceeds class default (6x).

intake_package.raw_protocol:
Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.

Substrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv
Michael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv
Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%
Solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v
Concentration: 0.1 M
Scale: 0.2 mmol

Step 1 - Giese radical addition:
The reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free
conditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for
4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a
in 92% yield.

Step 2 - Aerobic oxidation:
After Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was
continued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for another
6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.

Total batch reaction time: 10 hours
Final isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%

Critical requirements:
- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.

extracted_batch_fields.reaction_description: One-pot photoredox Giese radical addition (Step 1, argon, 4 h) followed by aerobic oxidation (Step 2, air, 6 h). Substrate PMPSCH2TMS (1a) with Michael acceptor acrylonitrile (2a) gives sulfide intermediate 3a (92% yield after Step 1), which is further oxidized to sulfoxide 4a (95% final isolated yield). Oxygen excluded in Step 1; air introduced after Step 1. pH 9 buffer suppresses PMPSCH3 byproduct formation.
extracted_batch_fields.raw_text:
Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.

Substrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv
Michael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv
Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%
Solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v
Concentration: 0.1 M
Scale: 0.2 mmol

Step 1 - Giese radical addition:
The reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free
conditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for
4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a
in 92% yield.

Step 2 - Aerobic oxidation:
After Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was
continued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for another
6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.

Total batch reaction time: 10 hours
Final isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%

Critical requirements:
- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.
- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.
- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.
- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct.

Oxygen excluded in Step 1; air introduced after Step 1. pH 9 buffer suppresses PMPSCH3 byproduct formation.",

  "raw_text": "Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.\n\nSubstrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv\nMichael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv\nPhotocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%\nSolvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v\nConcentration: 0.1 M\nScale: 0.2 mmol\n\nStep 1 - Giese radical addition:\nThe reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free\nconditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 \u00b0C for\n4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a\nin 92% yield.\n\nStep 2 - Aerobic oxidation:\nAfter Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was\ncontinued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 \u00b0C for another\n6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.\n\nTotal batch reaction time: 10 hours\nFinal isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%\n\nCritical requirements:\n- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.\n- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.\n- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.\n- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct."

steps.name: Kinetics & Residence Time
steps.summary: τ = 8.3 min (council-approved — not re-derived from kinetics). Implied IF = 72× vs batch.
assumptions: τ set by ENGINE council — kinetics estimation bypassed

steps.name: Reactor Sizing
steps.summary: V_R = 5.00 mL, d = 1.00 mm, L = 6.37 m, Pe = 96 (⚠ axial dispersion)
warnings: Pe = 96 < 100 — significant axial dispersion. Reactor behaves closer to CSTR than PFR. Reduce d (smaller d → higher Pe) or accept lower conversion efficiency.

steps.name: Mass Transfer
steps.summary: t_mix = 101.3 s, Da = 6.016 — Transition zone — mixing becoming significant
warnings: Da = 6.02 > 1: mixing may limit conversion. Consider static mixer insert.
assumptions: D = 1e-09 m²/s (typical for small organic molecules in liquid)
Gas holdup estimated from actual reactor gas/liquid volumetric ratio.
O2 solubility uses a water/ethanol-scale Henry-law approximation; validate experimentally for final scale-up.
kLa is a conservative capillary slug-flow estimate tied to gas holdup.

steps.name: Heat Transfer
steps.summary: Q_gen = 0.0882 W, Q_rem = 59.9991 W, Da_th = 0.0015 — Thermally safe

steps.name: Back-Pressure Regulator
steps.summary: BPR REQUIRED: 3.0 bar (Gas-liquid system detected — BPR mandatory to maintain gas solubility (Henry's law: C_gas = H·P) and prevent uncontrolled degassing.)
equations: C_{\mathrm{gas}} = H \cdot P_{\mathrm{partial}}\quad\text{(higher BPR} \Rightarrow \text{more dissolved gas)}

_analogies.summary: This photoredox catalysis process involves a radical addition followed by oxidation using fac-[Ir(ppy)3] as the photocatalyst with 425 nm LED irradiation. The reaction was performed in DMSO solvent at 25°C using a MiChS flow photoreactor L-1 (M) with 2 mm ID quartz tubing and a 2.7 mL reactor volume. The flow process achieved a remarkable 30-minute residence time at 0.09 mL/min flow rate, compared to 24 hours required in batch conditions. Flow chemistry provided dramatic improvements with a 48-fold reduction in reaction time (from 24 hours to 30 minutes) and a substantial increase in yield from 22% in batch to 75% in flow. The enhanced performance in flow resulted from improved light penetration and better mass transfer in the thin quartz tubing, enabling more efficient photocatalytic activation and faster reaction kinetics.

_analogies.summary: This photoredox cross-coupling reaction utilizes single electron transfer (SET) mechanism with Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photocatalyst (2 mol%) and tBu-TMG base in DMF solvent under 440 nm blue LED irradiation. The optimized flow process operates at 50°C with a 12-minute residence time at 0.83 mL/min flow rate in a segmented flow reactor using FEP tubing with 10 mL reactor volume. Flow conditions achieved 88% yield compared to 81% yield under batch conditions at 30°C, representing an 8.6% improvement in yield. The primary advantage of flow was enabling higher operating temperature (50°C vs 30°C) with superior heat transfer control, while providing predictable scale-up capability to hundreds of mg/h production rates with significantly shorter reaction times.

_analogies.summary: This photocatalyzed radical addition employs 2-benzopyrylium intermediates generated in situ as the photoredox catalyst under 450 nm LED irradiation. The flow process operates in a 1.0 mL photochemical reactor using 1,2-dichloroethane as solvent at room temperature (25°C) with a 2.5 minute residence time and 24.0 mL/min flow rate, achieving 77% yield. In contrast, the batch baseline required elevated temperature (50°C) and 60 minutes reaction time to obtain 76% yield. Flow processing provided a 24-fold intensification in reaction rate while maintaining comparable yield and enabling safer room temperature operation, demonstrating superior scalability for this photoredox transformation.

pre_council_proposal.residence_time_basis: liquid-only reactor volume / liquid flow rate. Stage 1: V_R1=10 mL / Q_liq=0.167 mL/min = 59.9 min. Stage 2 (liquid-only component): V_R2=10 mL / Q_liq=0.167 mL/min = 59.9 min (gas-liquid segmented flow; liquid-phase residence time reported; total two-stage liquid τ = ~120 min). Reported residence_time_min is per-stage liquid τ = 60 min. Total process τ = 120 min.
pre_council_proposal.light_setup: Vapourtec UV-150 450 nm module (KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450); 450 nm measured; 24 W radiant power; 355 mW/cm2 irradiance. UV-150 set to additional cooling mode to reach 25°C. Stage 1: 10 mL PFA coil in UV-150 cartridge (within 10 mL max). Stage 2: 10 mL FEP coil — if second UV-150 slot available, use same 450 nm module; if not, use KHU manual blue photoreactor (448 nm, 62 mW/cm2, fan mode 40°C) as fallback for Stage 2 with extended τ.
pre_council_proposal.deoxygenation_method: Offline Ar sparge of complete reagent solution in sealed reservoir (≥20 min), maintained under Ar positive pressure throughout Stage 1. No inline degasser used (hard constraint: forbidden equipment).

streams.pump_role: Main liquid feed pump — delivers pre-mixed, pre-degassed substrate/catalyst/acceptor solution to reactor inlet
streams.solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer 5:1 v/v, pre-degassed offline by Ar sparge, held in sealed reservoir
streams.reasoning: Chemistry Plan stream A: all liquid-phase reagents pre-mixed in one degassed reservoir. No reaction occurs in the dark so premixing is safe. Limiting reagent PMPSCH2TMS at 0.1 M; acrylonitrile at 0.2 M in same solution. Catalyst at 0.5 mol% dissolved homogeneously. Flow rate set so that Q_liq = 0.167 mL/min gives τ_liquid = 10 mL / 0.167 = ~60 min for Stage 1 (anaerobic coil). This is within the calculation range [11.1–150.0 min] and is deliberately set at the upper-middle end to bias toward maximized conversion given the kinetics uncertainty (Da=1.75 warning, class IF=6x vs analogy IF=21x disagreement). Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump (KHU-PUMP-VAPOURTEC-R-SERIES) used — compatible with Vapourtec UV-150, handles aqueous/EtOH, 0.01–10 mL/min, max 42 bar, well above ΔP=2.76 bar.

streams.pump_role: O2 gas feed via MFC — introduces oxygen between Stage 1 and Stage 2 for aerobic sulfide oxidation
streams.reasoning: Chemistry Plan stream B: O2 introduced only after Stage 1 outlet, at a T-junction before Stage 2 coil. Calculation: O2 MFC setpoint = 1.12 sccm (from engineering design step, gas equiv target 1.0–2.0 equiv O2). MFC range 0.01–10 sccm — 1.12 sccm is well within range. O2 must be strictly absent in Stage 1 (radical quenching). O2 segmented flow in Stage 2 provides excellent gas-liquid mass transfer (high kLa) for singlet-O2 sensitization pathway. BPR downstream of Stage 2 maintains pressure to keep O2 dissolved (Henry's law). KHU-GAS-MFC-O2-BRONKHORST assigned.

pre_council_proposal.mixer_type: T-junction (O2 gas into liquid stream between Stage 1 and Stage 2 coils)
pre_council_proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan mixing_order_reasoning: All liquid reagents (stream A) are pre-mixed offline in the dark — no reaction occurs without light, so PMPSCH2TMS, acrylonitrile, and Ir catalyst are stable together in solution. This single-feed approach avoids any premixing issues. O2 (stream B) is introduced only at the inter-stage T-junction, after the Stage 1 anaerobic coil outlet and before Stage 2 coil inlet. This is the critical sequencing requirement: O2 would quench the alpha-thio carbon radical in Stage 1, destroying Giese selectivity. The T-junction gas-liquid mixing point is positioned between the two reactor coils, both of which are irradiated under the same 450 nm UV-150 module.
pre_reactor_steps: OFFLINE DEGASSING (mandatory, hard constraint): Prepare the EtOH/pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v) solvent mixture and dissolve all reagents (PMPSCH2TMS 1.0 equiv, acrylonitrile 2.0 equiv, Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 0.5 mol%) to give 0.1 M solution. Sparge the sealed reservoir with dry argon for ≥20 min. Cap and maintain under Ar positive pressure throughout Stage 1. No inline degasser is available or permitted (hard constraint Q-CONSTR-001).

RESERVOIR SEALING: Transfer degassed solution to a sealed syringe reservoir or Schlenk-type vessel under Ar. Connect to pump inlet via Ar-purged transfer line. Verify no headspace O2 before starting flow.

LIGHT SOURCE WARM-UP: Power on Vapourtec UV-150 450 nm module (KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450) and allow LED to stabilize for 5 min before starting flow. Set UV-150 to additional cooling mode to achieve 25°C (within 10–35°C additional cooling range per photoreactor_limits).

SYSTEM PRIMING (Stage 1): Prime Stage 1 PFA 10 mL coil with degassed solution at 0.167 mL/min under Ar atmosphere. Allow 3× τ (3 × 60 min = 180 min) startup waste (~30 mL) before collecting. Note: startup waste is high due to large reactor volume; this is acceptable for a maximized-yield screening run.

MFC VERIFICATION: Set Bronkhorst O2 MFC to 1.12 sccm. Verify MFC outlet pressure compatible with BPR setpoint (7 bar). Do not open O2 to reactor until Stage 1 priming is complete and steady-state confirmed.
post_reactor_steps: BPR PRESSURE HOLD: Maintain 7 bar BPR (KHU-BPR-FIXED-7BAR) downstream of Stage 2 coil throughout collection. This keeps O2 dissolved during Stage 2 (Henry's law) and prevents acrylonitrile degassing (bp 77°C).
COLLECTION: Collect product stream in a sealed vial under ambient atmosphere after BPR. Product is sulfoxide 4a in EtOH/buffer mixture.
LIGHT OFF / MFC OFF: After collection complete, turn off UV-150 module and close O2 MFC before flushing system. Flush with degassed EtOH to clear lines.

ANALYTICAL WORKUP: Dilute collected fraction for HPLC or NMR analysis. Compare to batch benchmark (95% yield sulfoxide 4a). Check for sulfide 3a intermediate (indicates incomplete Stage 2 oxidation — increase τ or O2 flow if present) and PMPSCH3 byproduct (indicates insufficient pH buffering).
pre_council_proposal.chemistry_notes: MECHANISM: Stage 1 (Giese radical addition, anaerobic): Ir(III) photoexcited to Ir(III)* at 450 nm → oxidative quenching SET with PMPSCH2TMS → alpha-thio carbon radical → Giese addition to acrylonitrile → adduct radical reduced by Ir(II) → sulfide 3a. O2 MUST be excluded — O2 traps carbon radicals faster than acrylonitrile addition (k_O2 ~10^9 M^-1s^-1). Stage 2 (aerobic oxidation): Ir(III)* sensitizes triplet O2 to singlet O2 via energy transfer (MLCT triplet energy ~60 kcal/mol >> singlet O2 at 22.5 kcal/mol) → singlet O2 oxidizes sulfide 3a to sulfoxide 4a. Both stages require 450 nm light and the same Ir catalyst. pH 9 buffer suppresses protodesilyation/PMPSCH3 byproduct. ANALOGY ANALYSIS: Analogy 1 (score 0.550): Chemically similar — Ir photoredox catalysis, radical addition, same catalyst metal class (Ir(ppy) family), same temperature (25°C). Key difference: Analogy 1 used fac-Ir(ppy)3 (reductive quenching) in DMSO, achieved 30 min residence time with 48x batch reduction from 24h batch. Our reaction uses Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)+ (oxidative quenching, stronger oxidant) in EtOH/water, 10h batch. Adjustment: the batch time ratio suggests similar flow intensification; 30 min from analogy directly applicable as Stage 1 residence time starting point. We use 60 min for Stage 1 (2x longer) to bias toward maximized conversion per design objective, accepting that analogy suggests 30 min may suffice. Analogy 2 (score 0.537): Chemically similar — same exact photocatalyst class Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6, SET mechanism, blue LED 440 nm. Key difference: different reaction (cross-coupling with Ni co-catalyst, not Giese), DMF solvent, 50°C flow temperature vs 25°C batch. 12 min residence time at 0.83 mL/min in 10 mL FEP. Adjustment: our reaction is at 25°C (same as our batch), same catalyst family, but different reaction type — 12 min is too short for our more complex two-stage chemistry. Analogy 3 (score 0.507): Chemically similar — 450 nm blue LED, radical addition photocatalysis, 25°C, Ar atmosphere, same concentration 0.1 M. Key difference: 2-benzopyrylium catalyst (not Ir), 1,2-dichloroethane solvent, achieved 2.5 min from 60 min batch (24x IF). Adjustment: 24x IF is consistent with our calculated 21x IF; validates the intensification factor estimate. However, reaction is simpler (single step, no gas-liquid stage). REACTOR CHOICE RATIONALE: Two-stage design uses the 10 mL PFA coil (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) for Stage 1 (anaerobic Giese, τ=60 min at 0.167 mL/min) in the UV-150 with 450 nm module. For Stage 2 (aerobic oxidation), the 10 mL FEP coil (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-10ML) is used with O2 segmented flow, also under UV-150 450 nm. CONSTRAINT CHECK: UV-150 maximum coil volume = 10 mL per cartridge slot. If only one UV-150 slot is available, Stage 1 (10 mL PFA) uses UV-150 and Stage 2 (10 mL FEP) uses the KHU manual photoreactor (448 nm, 62 mW/cm2, 40°C with fan) as a lower-intensity alternative — this is a feasible fallback but may require longer τ for Stage 2. Primary design assumes two UV-150 slots or serial coil arrangement. TEMPERATURE: 25°C required (batch protocol, all analogies). UV-150 additional cooling mode (10–35°C range) achieves this. PRESSURE: BPR at 7 bar maintains O2 solubility in Stage 2 and suppresses acrylonitrile volatility. 7 bar > calculated 3.3 bar requirement, provides adequate safety margin. FLOW REGIME: Re=7.8 (laminar, confirmed plug flow Pe=329). Da=1.75 (transition zone — mixing may limit; noted in engineering calculations). Conservative τ=60 min selected partly to address this. PUMP: Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump (KHU-PUMP-VAPOURTEC-R-SERIES) selected for stream A — compatible with UV-150 system, handles EtOH/aqueous mixtures, 0.01–10 mL/min range covers 0.167 mL/min, max 42 bar >> operating pressure.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Calculation range: 11.1–150.0 min (blended analogy IF=21x). Analogy 1 gives 30 min (48x IF from 24h batch, Ir photoredox radical addition at 25°C — directly applicable mechanism). Analogy 3 gives 2.5 min (24x IF, but simpler single-step reaction). Calculation central estimate τ=28.6 min. Design objective is MAXIMIZED CONVERSION, so we select τ=60 min (upper-conservative within range) to ensure >95% conversion matching batch yield, given: (a) Da=1.75 warning from mixing calculations, (b) two-step sequential chemistry requiring both steps to reach completion, (c) kinetics uncertainty (6x vs 21x IF disagreement). 60 min is 2x analogy 1 value — conservative but justified for maximized yield objective. Total two-stage τ=120 min vs 10h batch = 5x intensification (conservative vs calculated 21x — appropriate given uncertainty).
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Liquid-only volume / liquid flow rate. In Stage 2 with gas-liquid segmented flow, the liquid occupies ~29% of channel (ε_g=0.71 from calculations), so actual liquid residence time in Stage 2 channel is longer per unit reactor volume, but the reported value uses nominal V_R/Q_liq for simplicity and safety margin. In-channel pressure-corrected time is slightly shorter (~55 min) due to gas compression at 7 bar BPR.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: 25°C — directly from batch protocol (hard constraint) and all three analogies (all operate at 25°C). UV-150 additional cooling mode achieves 10–35°C range, so 25°C is reachable. No thermal advantage gained by increasing temperature for this photoredox reaction; photon flux is the rate-limiting factor.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Engineering calculation: BPR required = 3.3 bar (gas-liquid system). Available fixed BPR options: 1.5, 2.5, 7.0, 8.0, 16.0 bar. Nearest above 3.3 bar is 7.0 bar (KHU-BPR-FIXED-7BAR). Selected 7.0 bar: (a) above minimum 3.3 bar requirement, (b) provides additional O2 solubility enhancement (Henry's law: higher pressure = more dissolved O2 for Stage 2 oxidation), (c) suppresses acrylonitrile volatility (bp 77°C at 1 bar; at 7 bar dissolved), (d) well within pump max 42 bar. Total system pressure = BPR 7 bar + ΔP 2.76 bar = 9.76 bar — within Vapourtec R-series 42 bar limit. MFC outlet max 9 bar — compatible with 7 bar BPR operating pressure.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: Stage 1: PFA (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) — UV-transparent, max 80°C, max 34 bar, compatible with UV-150 cartridge (≤10 mL). PFA preferred over FEP for UV-150 because max T=80°C vs FEP 50°C, giving better thermal headroom. Stage 2: FEP (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-10ML) — UV-transparent, suitable for gas-liquid O2 segmented flow, max 50°C adequate for 25°C operation. FEP has slightly better O2 permeability than PFA which is a minor benefit for aerobic stage. Both materials chemically compatible with EtOH/aqueous/acrylonitrile/TMS silane reagents.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.1 M — directly from batch protocol. Analogy 1: concentration not specified. Analogy 2: 0.05 M (lower, but different reaction type). Analogy 3: 0.1 M (exact match). No adjustment needed; 0.1 M is appropriate for photoredox catalysis at this scale, gives adequate photon penetration at 1 mm ID (Beer-Lambert: absorbance at 0.1 M with Ir loading 0.0005 M is dominated by substrate transparency at 450 nm).
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 has MLCT absorption with tail to ~460 nm; peak excitation ~380 nm but significant absorption at 450 nm. Batch uses 452 nm 10W LED. UV-150 450 nm module (measured 450 nm) at 355 mW/cm2 is the best inventory match — 35.5x higher irradiance than batch (10W over pressure tube ~10 mW/cm2 estimated) combined with ~20x higher S/V ratio = ~700x more photons per molecule. This drives the predicted 21x residence time reduction. No other UV-150 module is closer to 452 nm with comparable power (470 nm is off-peak; 420 nm is 30 nm blue-shifted but still on MLCT tail at 243 mW/cm2 — secondary option if 450 nm unavailable).
reasoning_per_field.deoxygenation_method: Hard constraint: no inline degasser permitted. Only allowed method: pre-degassed solvent offline. Ar sparge ≥20 min reduces dissolved O2 to <0.1 ppm (literature validated for similar aqueous/EtOH systems). Sealed Ar reservoir maintained throughout Stage 1. This is sufficient for Stage 1 radical chemistry.

safety_flags: O2_gas_in_flammable_solvent_system: EtOH is flammable; O2 at 7 bar creates elevated fire/explosion risk. Verify all fittings and connections are leak-tight before introducing O2. Use appropriate O2-compatible materials (PFA/FEP tubing confirmed compatible). Conduct O2 introduction in a well-ventilated fume hood.
acrylonitrile_volatility: bp 77°C, toxic, volatile. BPR at 7 bar suppresses evaporation. Handle in fume hood. Sealed reservoir required.
Ir_photocatalyst_light_sensitivity: protect catalyst solution from ambient light during preparation. Store in amber vials.
gas_liquid_pressure_buildup: BPR at 7 bar required downstream. Verify all coil and fitting pressure ratings (PFA/FEP max 34 bar — adequate). Pump max 42 bar — adequate. Do not block BPR outlet.

Stage1_O2_exclusion_critical: If O2 contamination occurs in Stage 1 (leak in Ar seal), radical quenching will give low yield and PMPSO2H byproducts. Monitor by inline or offline HPLC before advancing to Stage 2 collection.

blocking_reasons.message: No available certified gas-liquid mixer is listed.
The chemistry requires 2 sequential reaction stages, but no listed reactor train provides the required interstage topology.
